game_design_concept.title: The Journey
game_design_concept.elevator_pitch: A dark sci-fi action shooter where you battle mutant enemies across a procedurally-generated alien desert, fighting your way toward a hostile citadel. Master dynamic combat, tactical movement, and weapon switching to survive in a desolate, storm-lit world.
game_design_concept.art_style: Dark Sci-Fi Realism with Desaturated Palette
core_mechanics: Wall-assisted double jump for vertical traversal
Intelligent enemy AI with pathfinding and predictive interception
Ragdoll physics and blood decals on impact
Health system with damage feedback vignette
game_design_concept.setting_theme: A desolate alien desert under a low-hanging sun, featuring red sand dunes, ancient ruins, and mysterious technological structures. A hostile citadel looms in the distance as wind blows across the barren landscape, creating an atmosphere of impending confrontation and isolation.
game_design_concept.player_experience: Tense, tactical combat in a harsh alien environment. Players feel the weight of survival as they manage resources, navigate treacherous terrain, and engage intelligent enemies. The golden-hour lighting and ominous atmosphere create a sense of dread and urgency.
game_design_concept.target_audience: Core gamers aged 16+, fans of tactical shooters and sci-fi action games, players who enjoy challenging AI and resource management
game_design_concept.unique_hook: Combines dynamic first-person/third-person combat with procedurally-generated desert exploration and intelligent enemy AI that adapts to player tactics. The atmospheric sci-fi aesthetic and emphasis on tactical movement create a grounded, immersive survival experience.
game_design_concept.narrative_elements: The player is traversing a hostile alien world toward a mysterious citadel, battling mutant creatures and navigating ancient ruins. The narrative is environmental and atmospheric rather than story-driven, with the world itself telling the story of a desolate, contested landscape.
game_design_concept.technical_scope: Multi-level procedurally-generated world with dynamic physics, advanced AI systems, and real-time combat mechanics across a large explorable desert environment

core_gameplay_loop.name: Engage Enemy
core_gameplay_loop.description: Spot and target mutant enemies using tactical positioning and weapon selection

core_gameplay_loop.name: Manage Resources
core_gameplay_loop.description: Switch weapons, manage ammo, and collect pickups while maintaining tactical advantage

core_gameplay_loop.name: Execute Maneuvers
core_gameplay_loop.description: Dodge, crouch, jump, and slide to evade enemy fire and reposition for attacks

core_gameplay_loop.name: Eliminate Threat
core_gameplay_loop.description: Land shots with ranged weapons or close-range melee to defeat enemies

core_gameplay_loop.name: Navigate Forward
core_gameplay_loop.description: Move across procedurally-generated terrain toward the distant hostile citadel

style_guide.created_for: The Journey — A first-person/third-person sci-fi action shooter set in a dark alien desert with procedurally-generated terrain, dynamic combat, and hostile AI enemies.
style_guide.description: A desaturated, atmospheric sci-fi aesthetic dominated by warm golden-hour sand tones contrasting against cool indigo night skies and deep shadows. The world is deliberately dark and grounded, with structures rendered in concrete and steel to maximize combat readability against bright sand. Cyan-blue technology accents provide the only cool color relief. Custom fog, height-based density, and a luminous horizon band create an ominous, siege-like atmosphere. The visual language prioritizes clarity for fast-paced combat while maintaining an immersive, hostile alien environment.
mood_references: Blade Runner 2049 — desaturated color grading and atmospheric haze
DOOM Eternal — dark sci-fi structures and combat readability
Stalker — ominous alien atmosphere and environmental storytelling
style_guide.notes: Maintain high contrast between sand (primary visual element) and structures (secondary) to ensure combat readability. Cyan accents should be used sparingly for technology and UI to avoid visual noise. Fog and haze are critical for atmosphere—adjust density based on distance and height. All lighting should emphasize the low-hanging sun's warm glow against cool shadows. Procedural terrain should use noise-based variation in sand tones within the #ccaa80 to #8a6a52 range. Enemy ragdoll and blood effects should use desaturated reds to maintain visual cohesion.
